items.prompt:
The sentence that states a paragraph's main point is the:
A) topic sentence
B) title
C) footnote

Sentences that explain or prove the main idea are:
A) supporting sentences
B) titles
C) citations

A sentence that wraps up a paragraph is the:
A) concluding sentence
B) topic sentence
C) heading

Read.

(1) Honeybees are vital pollinators. (2) They fertilize a third of our crops. (3) Without them, many foods would vanish.

Sentence (1) is the:
A) topic sentence
B) concluding sentence
C) off-topic sentence

steps: States main point. Key is A.

items.prompt:
In that paragraph, sentences (2) and (3) mainly:
A) support and develop the main point
B) change the topic
C) contradict sentence 1
items.answer: A) support and develop the main point

solution.answer: A) support and develop the main point

items.prompt:
A sentence that adds a precise statistic to a paragraph serves to:
A) provide supporting evidence
B) end the essay
C) restate the title

Read.

(1) Many assume all fats are unhealthy. (2) In fact, some fats are essential. (3) For example, omega-3s support brain function.

The role of sentence (2) is to:
A) refine the key concept by correcting a misconception
B) restate sentence 1 exactly
C) change the subject
items.answer: A) refine the key concept by correcting a misconception

solution.answer: A) refine the key concept by correcting a misconception

items.prompt:
Analyzing the STRUCTURE of a paragraph means examining:
A) the role each sentence plays in developing the key concept
B) only the word count
C) only the first letter
items.answer: A) the role each sentence plays in developing the key concept

solution.answer: A) the role each sentence plays in developing the key concept
